pr_title: Include the query type and name in all c-ares DNS error messages
pr_body:
Fixes #21308.

Includes query type (e.g. "A", "AAAA", "SRV", "TXT"), and target name in potentially-surfaced errors. This additional context should help debugging DNS related errors with and without trace logs enabled. I've found myself wondering what e.g. the particular query type a c-ares tracer log line corresponded to more than once.

issue_context.title: dns resolution failed: which address?
issue_context.body: I'm currently getting "DNS resolution failed" errors. It would be better if the error was, "DNS resolution failed for address <whatever.com>". This would help debugging _immensely_.
comments: Mark, can you take a look at this?
Why is this useful?  Don't you know what server name you used when you created the channel?

In client libraries, you can set the endpoint to connect to in a number of ways:

- It may be hard-coded in some layer of the client libraries
- You may be able to set an env var such as `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST`
- You may be able to pass in options; there may be overlapping options that deal with endpoint
- (etc)

The dial may be many layers below the publicly-visible API. So, when a user supplies several addresses, it can be really hard to debug what's going on and which is trying to be used: they have no idea where the dial is and probably don't have the ability to modify that code to put in logging. I think this is a compelling reason.

Moreover, though, I think it's just sensible: it's hardly any more information in the error message and it turns the error into a far-more debuggable form. In Go's stdlib, the address is shown in error messages; as in `curl`, and many other libraries and applications that target endpoints.

This would help us tremendously. We have chains of RPCs bubbling errors up from one end to the other, and these errors are really hard to track without having to intercept and rewrite errors every stage of the way.

This issue/PR has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had any update (including commits, comments, labels, milestones, etc) for 30 days. It will be closed automatically if no further update occurs in 7 day. Thank you for your contributions!

WIP on this in #22865

Note that that error message will appear in gRPC library logs (before that PR, today, this information shows up in gRPC library logs when `GRPC_VERBOSITY=DEBUG` and `GRPC_TRACE=cares_resolver,cares_address_sorting` are set). 

But in order for those errors to be surfaced to wrapped language layers (e.g. in wrapped language Exception objects etc.), we'd need to confirm that they surface this error string: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/e29f3b27b18717c7c3dba27c3bd4008200f01390/include/grpc/impl/codegen/grpc_types.h#L675. Is there a particular wrapped language this was most important for?
IIRC it was for python, but I don't remember super well. :)

Alex, your PR is improving the trace logging, but I think this issue is asking about including the information in the error message we return when an individual RPC fails.

C-core in general doesn't do a good job of accumulating the right set of useful information to include in status messages.  I think we need to do a full audit of the client channel code and improve this.  There will probably be some internal API changes involved; for example, we will need to pass some additional state from the resolver to the LB policy in order to do this effectively.

Unfortunately, this is a fair amount of work but is not high priority right now, so I'm not sure when we'll get to this.

Mark, note my PR #22865 affects not only the trace logging but also messages in the `grpc_error` objects returned by c-ares.

I've confirmed it's visible at the surface layer in the [recv_status_op.error_string](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/67bafdfc9cca245a2a368d368e99675ff36638a3/include/grpc/impl/codegen/grpc_types.h#L675) field.

So if an RPC is failed with a `grpc_errror` object created by the resolver, then the detailed error string will be available in that `recv_status_op` field.

For example, in C++, it ends up getting surfaced to the user in the `debug_error_string()` field of the `ClientContext`. The interop clients logs that field from [here](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/67bafdfc9cca245a2a368d368e99675ff36638a3/test/cpp/interop/interop_client.cc#L140):

```
apolcyn@apolcyn0:~/grpc$ bins/dbg/interop_client --server_host=foo.does.not.exist --server_port=443 
D0506 09:13:16.065025790   45642 test_config.cc:386]         test slowdown factor: sanitizer=1, fixture=1, poller=1, total=1
I0506 09:13:16.065210984   45642 client.cc:165]              Testing these cases: large_unary
E0506 09:13:16.367136323   45642 interop_client.cc:138]      Error status code: 14 (expected: 0), message: DNS resolution failed, debug string: {"created":"@1588781596.366803346","description":"Failed to pick subchannel","file":"src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/client_channel.cc","file_line":3936,"referenced_errors":[{"created":"@1588781596.366784403","description":"Resolver transient failure","file":"src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/resolving_lb_policy.cc","file_line":212,"referenced_errors":[{"created":"@1588781596.366780734","description":"DNS resolution failed","file":"src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/resolver/dns/c_ares/dns_resolver_ares.cc","file_line":374,"grpc_status":14,"referenced_errors":[{"created":"@1588781596.366668271","description":"C-ares status is not ARES_SUCCESS qtype=A name=foo.does.not.exist is_balancer=0: Domain name not found","file":"src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/resolver/dns/c_ares/grpc_ares_wrapper.cc","file_line":264,"referenced_errors":[{"created":"@1588781596.366653758","description":"C-ares status is not ARES_SUCCESS qtype=AAAA name=foo.does.not.exist is_balancer=0: Domain name not found","file":"src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/resolver/dns/c_ares/grpc_ares_wrapper.cc","file_line":264}]}]}]}]}
```

And e.g. I realized that Ruby doesn't surface that field, so am surfacing it in https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/22876

Ah, okay -- I didn't notice that that PR also affected the returned error.  That's definitely helpful.

That having been said, that's not a complete fix, because the error from the resolver is included in the call's status only when the initial resolution attempt(s) fail.  Once a resolution attempt succeeds and an LB policy is created, the LB policy is responsible for setting the error message, and it no longer has access to the error from the resolver.  So, for example, if the resolver returns no addresses, pick_first will simply return an error that says ["Empty update"](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/67bafdfc9cca245a2a368d368e99675ff36638a3/src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/lb_policy/pick_first/pick_first.cc#L200).  That error should also include details about the resolver failure, but those details are not currently visible at that layer of the code.

I'm reassigning this to Donna, since she will probably work on this eventually as part of the client channel principles revamp.

Since the original issue was filed about RPCs that failed with "DNS resolution failed" [error messages](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/7b3590d5437df4c3492d2ca3ca76d89e6cd0a7ff/src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/resolver/dns/c_ares/dns_resolver_ares.cc#L375), which are only generated by DNS resolvers, I think #22865 will fully address at least the case that this specific problem this issue was originally filed about - when DNS resolution fails on a new channel. 

Plumbing more error context through the client channel in all cases sounds good to me, but should we create a separate tracking issue for that, since that's more broad in scope?
Okay.  I've filed #22883 to track the more general problem.

review_comments: I don't understand the purpose of this class.  It seems to be a simple wrapper of `grpc_ares_request`, but it doesn't seem to provide any functionality that isn't already present in the latter.  Why is this wrapper being added?

My idea here was that a `GrpcAresQuery` tracks fields that are particular to a single c-ares query (or "search") - e.g. a single A, AAAA, SRV, or TXT resolution performed by the c-ares APIs. A `grpc_ares_request`, on the other hand, tracks fields that are necessary to drive a complete DNS resolution process - which consists of multiple "child" queries.

So, the main thing is that a `grpc_ares_request` and a `GrpcAresQuery` differ in scope and lifetime - the former is per-grpc-resolution and the latter is per-c-ares-query.

Alternatively we could just put the SRV target name and TXT target name as additional fields into the `grpc_ares_request`, but keeping them separate seemed cleaner (I think this will become more important after making `grpc_ares_hostbyname_request` a sub-type of `GrpcAresQuery`).

Okay, I guess this is fine for now.  I would like to find a cleaner way to do this that does not require allocating so many different data structures, but I guess we can optimize that as part of the larger C++ conversion.  For now, please add a TODO about this.
